title: Microflow stream gateways and typed action surface — PRD draft
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD-level draft exploring a compact runtime+SDK pattern we call "microflow stream gateways". Objective is to enable low-latency partial-streaming with deterministic typed actions (tool calls / structured JSON outputs) while keeping client SDK ergonomics friendly for web and server environments.

Problem statement:
- Customers want the latency and interactivity of streaming for UX (early partial responses, progress indicators) but also need strong guarantees for tool calling (idempotency, typed args) and structured output (schemas, validation).
- Existing streaming surfaces mix freeform text and ad-hoc JSON emits; developers end up doing brittle client parsing, complex reconciliation, and poor error handling when partial frames mismatch final output.
- We need an SDK-friendly surface that: 1) surfaces partial text early, 2) emits typed action frames reliably, 3) supports resumable sessions and prefetch/hinting, and 4) integrates with hosted API runtime fallbacks.

Goals (measurable):
- Latency: first-byte latency for streaming microflow responses <= 60ms p50 in hosted regions for typical 2048 token models.
- Developer Ergonomics: reduce client-side parsing error rate in internal playtests by 80% vs current ad-hoc streaming experiments.
- Reliability: typed action frames should be delivered exactly-once (or have a clearly documented idempotent retry token) in >= 99.95% of requests at steady state.
- Adoption: ship a minimal SDK surface used by at least 2 internal reference apps within 6 weeks of feature stabilization.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full session-state replication for Dedicated/Private deployments (we assume persisted session metadata will be an opt-in layer later).
- Full typed-schema migrations/versioning in launch (we provide schema tags and a fallback strategy but not an elaborate migration API).

High-level approach:
- Introduce a light-weight gateway concept at the server side: each user request may open a "microflow gateway" session with a short-lived ID. Gateways coordinate: partial-token streaming, typed action frames, prefetch hints, and final commit.
- Streaming protocol: keep the wire format as newline-delimited frames over HTTP/1.1 SSE or HTTP/2/3 streaming. Each frame is a small envelope with a frame_type and monotonic frame_id. Frame types: partial_text, typed_action, meta, checkpoint, error.
- Typed action contract: actions are JSON objects conforming to an author-provided schema reference (schema_id). Each typed_action frame includes: action_id, schema_id, args, idempotency_token, status. Clients must be able to request action replays by action_id.
- SDK ergonomics: provide small, consistent streaming client APIs for JS and Python that decode frames, validate typed_action against lightweight schema (server-supplied), and surface a clear callback model for partial_text vs typed_action vs final. SDKs include automatic retry/backoff for lost connections and a resume token tied to gateway_id + checkpoint_id.

API sketch (HTTP + streaming frames):
- POST /v1/microflow/run
  body: { prompt, model, gateway_options: {prefetch: [schema_ids], initial_context_tokens: 64} }
  response: 200 (streaming) -> stream frames: {frame_type, frame_id, gateway_id, payload}

Example frames (JSON per line):
- {"frame_type":"partial_text","frame_id":1,"gateway_id":"gw_abc","payload":{"delta":"Sure— here\"s the plan:\n"}}
- {"frame_type":"typed_action","frame_id":4,"gateway_id":"gw_abc","payload":{"action_id":"a1","schema_id":"todo.v1","args":{"task":"draft PRD"},"idempotency_token":"tok-123","status":"ready"}}
- {"frame_type":"checkpoint","frame_id":5,"gateway_id":"gw_abc","payload":{"checkpoint_id":"cp_12","cursor_offset":128}}
- {"frame_type":"final","frame_id":9,"gateway_id":"gw_abc","payload":{"summary":"done","final_text":"..."}}

Client SDK examples (informal):
- JS (browser):
  const stream = await client.microflow.run({prompt, model});
  stream.on('partial', text => showProgress(text));
  stream.on('action', async action => {
    // validate or use schema helper
    if (action.schema_id === 'todo.v1') createTodo(action.args);
    stream.ackAction(action.action_id); // acknowledge delivery
  });
  stream.on('checkpoint', cp => saveResume(cp.checkpoint_id));
  stream.on('end', meta => finalize(meta));

- Python (server):
  with client.microflow.run(...) as it:
      for frame in it.frames():
          if frame.type == 'partial_text': buffer.append(frame.payload['delta'])
          elif frame.type == 'typed_action': process_action(frame.payload)

Operational semantics and safety:
- Exactly-once for typed_action is achieved via idempotency_token + server-ack semantics. The SDK will surface an ackAction call; if ackAction is not received (network fail), server retries will include the idempotency_token and server will dedupe.
- Checkpoints are consistent cut points; resume uses gateway_id + checkpoint_id. Resume semantics only guarantee monotonic consumption; clients must reconcile local side-effects (e.g., createTodo) using idempotency tokens.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit per-frame telemetry: frame_type, latency since prior frame, model_variant, gateway_id, checkpoint_latency.
- Add SDK-side counters: reconnections, resumed_sessions, action_ack_time, schema_validation_errors.
- Product dashboard: per-route traces showing first-frame latency, average frames-per-second, typed_action delivery success rate.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): implement gateway + frame emitter on runtime, JS and Python SDK adapters, integrate with two reference apps (chat agent and code assistant). Duration: 4 weeks.
- Beta (external opt-in): limited customers, metrics collection, add canary fallback to non-typed streaming. Duration: 6 weeks.
- GA: SDKs stable, migration docs, config flags for Dedicated/Private.

Migration and compatibility notes:
- Default behavior remains text-only streaming. Microflow is opt-in via gateway_options.
- For older SDKs, typed_action frames will be emitted as meta messages containing a schema link to avoid breaking clients.

Open questions / decisions (high priority):
- How strict should runtime validation be on typed_action args? Reject vs emit error frame and continue. Recommendation: soft-validation by default (emit typed_action + schema_validation_error frame) and a server flag for strict mode.
- Where do we store schema definitions for private deployments? Option: bundle schema registry endpoint per-tenant (requires infra work).
- Billing model: count microflow frames vs tokens? Recommend token-based billing with an optional small per-gateway metadata surcharge for guaranteed delivery SLAs.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- Eng: prototype frame envelope and checkpoint storage for ephemeral gateways (owner: Liam).
- SDK: produce minimal JS streaming wrapper that demuxes frames and exposes typed_action ack API (owner: Priya).
- Product: refine success metrics with two reference apps and write migration guide (owner: Avery).
- Security: threat model for idempotency_token replay and action injection (contact S&C).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: focuses on developer ergonomics and clear error modes. Please call out major incompatibilities with current runtime (esp. batching) and suggest alternate idempotency designs if you see scale issues.

References:
- internal experiment notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HOSTED/Microflow+Experiment+Notes
- design discussion: GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/3421
- tracking ticket: JIRA HOSTED-859
